details: Global oil prices have surged due to ongoing geopolitical tensions and uncertainty surrounding the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz. This rise is stoking renewed inflation concerns, leading to increased speculation about potential Federal Reserve interest rate hikes. Higher interest rates typically reduce the appeal of speculative assets like cryptocurrencies.
title: Oil Rally Stokes Inflation Fears, Weighs on Risk Assets

details: The United States Consumer Price Index (CPI) data for July is scheduled for release on August 12, 2026. This is a highly anticipated economic event that will significantly influence expectations for the Federal Reserve's monetary policy, particularly regarding future interest rate decisions. Economists anticipate a slight moderation in the year-over-year headline inflation rate but a potential increase in core CPI.
title: Crucial US July CPI Data Release Set for August 12

details: On August 10, US spot Bitcoin Exchange-Traded Funds (ETFs) recorded $144.6 million in net outflows, ending a five-day period of positive inflows. Additionally, Ether ETFs also experienced $14.6 million in net redemptions. This reversal in institutional demand suggests a pause in accumulation amidst a cautious macroeconomic environment.
title: Crypto ETFs See Outflows, Breaking Inflow Streak

details: The Digital Asset Market Clarity Act, a key piece of proposed crypto legislation, has stalled in the U.S. Senate. However, regulators are pressing ahead, with the SEC scheduled to vote on new rules for crypto offerings on August 14. Furthermore, CFTC Chairman Michael Selig has indicated that the agency is prepared to implement its own cryptocurrency regulations irrespective of congressional action.
title: SEC, CFTC Push Crypto Rules Amid Clarity Act Stall
